quest.title: Cry From the Eleazar Hospital
quest.description: After arresting the Radicals together with Dehya, you escorted them back to Aaru Village. The testimony revealed the involvement of a mysterious man and his forces. At the same time, Alhaitham has appeared in front of the village chief's house...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

chapter.title: King Deshret and the Three Magi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get some food in us, and then we'll— Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did you come from?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, as you can see, I am merely sitting here and reviewing what we have deduced thus far.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were gone for ages, and now you're suddenly sitting here musing to yourself? Where have you been, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's with the silence!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You never think things through before asking questions. I'm giving you some time to make up for that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Argh, Paimon's so mad! Paimon's gonna give you an ugly nickname!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go ahead, I won't stop you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, um... Never mind, Paimon's got nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's just nothing super obvious to pick with this guy... It makes it so hard.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, you've heard nothing to suggest I left this whole time. So clearly, I stayed in the village to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Anyway. You plan to leave Aaru Village and keep searching for the truth of this matter, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we're not gonna find out anything more by staying here. So we thought that we might as well take the search elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Enough with the silent treatment!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he's giving us time to think...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, I'm just surprised that you decided to team up with him.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, you haven't helped us out at all ever since we arrived at Aaru Village. Bold of you to question our choices.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! You're all talk!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: While you were investigating, I had my own work to do, which I've now finished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Paimon doesn't believe you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: To be honest, we aren't really a team, so I have no obligation to inform you of my whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not to mention that going separate ways allowed me to find some important information that you all had missed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Right here in the village?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What did you learn?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm going to take you to someone. But before that, you need to understand where she's coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: How do you think the residents of Aaru Village feel about what we're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In other words, do you truly believe every single word the villagers tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean... some of them lied to us?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hiding the truth does not necessarily equate to lying. Again, these people have their reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Remember what Candace said? Most people in Aaru Village don't necessarily care which deity is in charge of Sumeru. That's because whether King Deshret or the Dendro Archon has power is of little significance to them.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: By contrast, the perils of their daily lives are ever-present concerns. They won't simply share everything they know with you without good reason. That's why you believed there was no further information to be found in this village.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you're saying we can find new info from someone we've already spoken to.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Glad you're following along.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Among those you have talked to, there's someone who was consciously keeping you out of the loop. In fact, she's been observing your every move since you arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The reason being... To someone who only wants to live their life in peace, any external factors introduce unpredictability into the equation.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Whaaa! Those eyes, those fierce eyes! Y—You look like a real fighter...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't change the subject.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's quite obvious that she's intimidated by Cyno's authority and strength.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: R—Right! You were asking about the Vil— I mean, the mad scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: She corrected herself mid-sentence because she's aware that there are King Deshret fanatics in the village. If she sounds too friendly towards the Village Keepers, she could easily make herself the Radicals' next target.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: I think it's been a few days since I last saw them? I usually go to bed pretty early, so I'm not too familiar with what goes on at night.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Remember? She made a point of denying her involvement in anything that occurs at night.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: But honestly, I feel quite sympathetic towards them. Even though they act a little strange, they've helped me in the past. If it weren't for them, my house would've collapsed long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: After speaking to the village chief, it became clear that the Village Keepers had protected Aaru Village at night. In other words, the young miss was very much awake during that time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why would she lie?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: By getting involved with an outsider, she risks drawing unwanted attention to herself. As for why she might be so wary about all this... Maybe you should ask her.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll pass on this one.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You said that she is afraid of me. If so, it's best if I stay out of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're on it!

talks.objective: Look for the person mentioned by Alhaitham

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Miss Shani, as we discussed earlier, I've brought someone with me.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Mr. Alhaitham, I'm aware of where you stand, but... How can I make sure that your friends think the same as you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? We need to clarify our stance or something?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Go ahead and talk to her. You'll get the answers you want.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Go on, earn her trust.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it really that simple...?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Um, may I call you "Traveler"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure thing. Hi, Miss Shani.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Hi, Traveler. I want to ask you something.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Do you think the resurrection of King Deshret can truly change Sumeru for the better?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because it'll only result in conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: That's very similar to what Miss Candace says. I know you two are friends. That's why I'm willing to talk to you, even though I do have some reservations.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Before, I wouldn't even have the courage to ask something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Traveler, do you believe our lives will get better?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't promise anything. But I'll do the best I can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We came here from another nation, so it isn't wrong of you to be wary. And... we aren't really residents of any one nation...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But even so, we've met lots of people from different places and we've always fought for what we believed in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We have friends in Sumeru, and we want to help them... That's why we decided to stay here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: I... want to trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: My apologies for posing my questions like that. To be honest, I didn't expect you to come back for more information.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alhaitham told us you have your reasons. It's okay, we understand!

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: The fact is that I'm... Only one side of my family is desert folk. I don't really fit in anywhere in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Some believe in the Dendro Archon, while others believe in King Deshret. I don't belong to either side, and neither side would want me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, the Radicals mentioned that they despise traitors... Do they just think that anyone who's different from them is a traitor?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Yeah... Some people can be so narrow-minded when it comes to bloodline and beliefs... It makes no difference what I say or how I behave, I'll always be suspected of having ulterior motives.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Slowly, I just stopped talking to people. I pretended not to hear or see anything. All I want is to live my life in peace...

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: ...And then it happened. The Village Keepers who had helped me disappeared with no explanation, and I didn't dare breathe a word about it to anyone... until now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: #You can tell them. I'm sure {F#she}{M#he}'ll keep your secret.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Alright. I'll tell you what I told Alhaitham.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: I actually have a sharper sense of hearing than most. Sometimes... I hear strange crying sounds in the night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! There are ghosts!?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: Perhaps. I'm not sure. It's faint, but it's definitely the sound of crying. It comes from far away in the distance, and always carries very raw emotion.

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: It used to be louder and more frequent, but ever since you arrived in the village, it doesn't seem to happen as often, and when it does, it's much quieter. I have to focus really hard to make it out.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I confirmed this with the guards on night duty. They also have someone with a good ear, and he's heard similar sounds at night.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But because we're in the middle of a desert, he would rather believe that they are the cries of beasts than ghosts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you make out where the sounds were coming from?

dialogues.speaker: Shani
dialogues.text: There's really nothing around these parts... except for an old hospital not far from the village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I think they used to use it for treating Eleazar... But it's been abandoned for years.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to check out that hospital!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... They were easier to deal with than Paimon had expected.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you even expecting?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... super strong bandits? Or monsters taller than buildings dropping out of the sky? Or y'know, something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He looks super serious... We gotta stay on our A-game, too!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...This is the one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's go in and take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You carefully search the abandoned hospital...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heeey! Alhaitham, we haven't found squat! Are you sure we aren't wasting our time here?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Patience. Shani says she only hears the crying at night. We have time to burn.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Until then...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm taking a break.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And just like that, he sits down... Wait, he even brought a book to read!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you reading? Let Paimon see!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Okay, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Umm... "The 'natural position,' which is the positional propensity of an entity in 'natural motion,' in contrast with an object in 'forced motion'... Huh? When free from external influences, every entity... displays the tendency to follow its natural trajectory..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So, you got that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gives up! You keep reading your book... See ya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is he so relaxed? Look at him, reading an impossible book in a creepy place like this.

choices.text: You know, it wouldn't kill you to read a book once in a while, either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Paimon's your Teyvat travel guide! Paimon knows plenty of useful stuff already!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And anyway, it's not Paimon's fault that the books people read in Sumeru are so complicated...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, okay, Paimon's the best.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *yawn* Paimon's getting so sleepy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What was that sound?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: There it is.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's coming from that direction.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is the sound coming from here? Paimon's not seeing anything.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's from below.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?! But there's no way we can get down there!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Something is off about the interior here.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: As I thought. There's a hidden structure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... It's like they tucked another hospital into this one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like there are other mechanisms around here. Let's keep exploring!

choices.text: Maybe it's time to spread your wings and become learned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what good is that gonna do for you? You're acting like one of those annoying grown-ups who go around nagging people to focus on their studies!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The more you learn, the more money you can earn to support me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what gives? Shouldn't you be the one providing for Paimon!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Isn't that what I'm doing now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right... Okay then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, thank you for working so hard and earning so much Mora... If it weren't for you, Paimon would probably still be floating around in the ocean somewhere... Hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: Please stay safe, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'll be awaiting your good news.

talks.objective: Investigate the Elemental Monuments around the hospital
Investigate the Elemental Monuments around the hospital
Investigate the Elemental Monuments around the hospital

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Whatever it takes? You just might be scholar material.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Eremites once said that I was a lunatic. Perhaps a little madness is essential to be successful in research.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Why does it feel like he's using his praise for me as an excuse to brag about himself?

choices.text: I think he was just stating the truth.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Okay, let's get moving. We should head back to the village and rest up. Today was just a trial run — noon tomorrow is gonna be the hard part.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You all return to Aaru Village and rest in your rooms in preparation for tomorrow's hostage exchange.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: But what are the chances of success? What are the stakes? There is no way of knowing...

talks.objective: Go to the lower level of the hospital
Talk to the people in front of you

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there's someone over there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to be careful!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea, let's approach him slowly without alarming him...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Wait...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You're...
Ugh... Argh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He can't speak, and his eyes are unfocused... But he looks too young to be anyone's grandfather.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, why's he the only one here?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Didn't expect to see him here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...You know him?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: He's Razak, a senior of mine at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's a scholar, too? Is he the kind that holes up in a forest and mumbles stuff about training?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, and that's the problem.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Razak was never involved in any of those things. He never trained in the forest, let alone reached Satyavada Life.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So how did he become like this?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Leaving that question aside for the moment... him being here alone means that we might be too late.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like they've already taken everyone away. For whatever reason, they left Razak here — perhaps they simply didn't have time to come back for him.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There are drag marks on the ground. They're clearer by the doorway. Someone was forcefully drawing a cart that was loaded with something heavy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Loaded with... people?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That is one possibility. It looks like they were in a hurry, as if they were afraid of being caught. In their haste, they failed to notice Razak hiding in a corner.

dialogues.speaker: Razak
dialogues.text: Aah... Ugh, uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The symptoms are identical. Looks like we've found "living proof."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Allow me to jog your memory. Recall your time at Port Ormos.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't you think his symptoms look familiar?

dialogues.speaker: Mizri
dialogues.text: Aaagh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...! The Eremite guy who went mad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Now that you mention it... They're acting the same way!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Correct. The Akademiya is behind all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It isn't difficult to deduce their rationale.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: First, the Akademiya spread a false rumor of King Deshret's resurrection, emphasizing the role of the Village Keepers — the mad scholars who were exiled to Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: These rumors were all the persuasion that the Radicals needed, and those based in Aaru Village leapt into action. Unbeknownst to them, of course, through rounding up the scholars, they were actually helping the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As well as being able to exploit the Radicals for their own ends, this scheme has one further advantage to the Akademiya: All the risks and responsibilities are offloaded onto King Deshret's followers.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Life for the desert-dwellers has been brutal ever since King Deshret's death all those years ago. Beneath the surface, feelings of desperation are widespread.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Many would give everything they have for the prospect of something better. Anyone looking to exploit that for their own ends simply needs to make a few empty promises.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Even if complications arise, people will see that those involved are all followers of King Deshret, and look for no further explanation than differences of belief. A deep-seated mistrust of the desert and everyone in it by the rest of Sumeru will make sure of that.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The notion of an Akademiya plot wouldn't even cross their minds. It may seem like a simple strategy, but it is able to work wonders under Sumeru's current circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, that makes a lot of sense. It's in line with the village chief's theory, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's still one very important question... Wasn't it the Akademiya that brought the scholars to Aaru Village in the first place? Why does it want them back now?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Throughout this process, one thing has changed: the scholars' identity.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: First, they were "scholars." Then, they became "lunatics." After that, they were "exiles," and finally... they become "missing persons."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: An exile is still patently a living, breathing human being, but when someone becomes a missing person... that is brought into question.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If you can't find someone, you have no way of knowing what exactly happened to them. That makes missing people an ideal resource.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Resource"? For what, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: One possibility is that the information in their brains could be extracted into Knowledge Capsules.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Extracted... You mean Canned Knowledge comes from people's brains!?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: With the technology of the Sumeru Akademiya, it's entirely possible.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Perhaps the process caused them great suffering, which is why they cry out in the dead of night, when no one is watching them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the human brain— Nope, nuh-uh, Paimon doesn't wanna think about this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you learn of this technology?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm the Akademiya's scribe, after all. I'm familiar with their projects.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Anyway, judging by Razak's state, the contents of a Divine Knowledge Capsule were extracted from his mind, but something went wrong in the process...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, his curiosity got the better of him, and he used such a capsule for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's a little confused... Can they just use anyone's brain?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (No, that can't be right. Most of the mad scholars had made contact with the "divine consciousness" in the forest... That's what the Akademiya is after.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's also safe to assume that... this knowledge has something to do with the Fatui, The Doctor, and also The Balladeer. They're using Divine Knowledge Capsules to turn The Balladeer into a god.)

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The look on your face tells me you've realized the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Akademiya needs people who have been exposed to the "divine consciousness."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's right. To some scholars, gaining knowledge about the gods is their entire life's pursuit. Extracting Canned Knowledge is just one of the extreme measures they turn to.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: However, I can't help but wonder: What do they seek to gain from divine knowledge?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akademiya is going out of their way to look for forbidden knowledge, but what is their ultimate goal?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I've spent quite some time trying to analyze the contents of the Divine Knowledge Capsule, but to no avail. It seems like my way of thinking is too different from theirs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, you're not even slightly interested in getting your hands on this forbidden stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: All scholars seek to expand the horizons of knowledge. But I'm not particularly interested in gods, so I don't share their degree of zealotry.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Extracting information from people as if they were lifeless objects... If this is the direction of academic progress, then the Akademiya may as well shut its doors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you're really against all this...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Of course. The Akademiya's actions run contrary to their rules.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Whether it be academics or knowledge, everything has its boundaries. If those lines are crossed, the rules and order that govern everything in the world will be destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This matter needs to be corrected, just like fixing a typo in a book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, didn't you step in to help because you felt sympathy for those poor people?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not to be callous, but no. My criteria are a little more restrictive than that.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There is no shortage of suffering in Sumeru, and the same can be said for the rest of Teyvat as well. What do you plan to do about that? Save every last person?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Probably not... Paimon's not sure...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your motives are more specific and personal.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You can say that. Simply put, I don't blindly place my faith into strength or heroism. I do what I want.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Divine Knowledge Capsule is something I want to investigate in full. That doesn't mean I'm willing to take action for the sake of a few strangers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Though he rejects the notion of greater moral responsibility, he justifies his actions because they are true to his personal motivations.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Someone like him... might actually make for a better ally.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's been wanting to say this for a while. There are a lot of bad guys in the Akademiya, but you're not one of them... You're their weirdo!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...You're probably right.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Though I must say, I quite enjoy this feeling of being the odd one out.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Uniqueness is also an asset, is it not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's a great way to think about it. Paimon's really impressed! If only Miss Shani had a similar mindset, her life would definitely be a lot easier...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm just a more likable person than her in general. There's nothing more to it than that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, so what do we do with him?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: He won't last long if we leave him here. Let's take him with us.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We'll work out our next step after we return to Aaru Village.

talks.objective: Go back to the village chief's house and meet up with everybody else

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You must be tired. You should rest, and take some water.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hmm? Who's this?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, somebody who is too young to take on the role of Isak's grandfather. Nevertheless, he's one of the people we're trying to find.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell everyone what you saw in the abandoned hospital and share your current theory.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So, at one point in time, the abandoned Eleazar hospital served as the Akademiya's site for extracting Divine Canned Knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, pretty much.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Their plan must have been implemented at some point before we arrived at Aaru Village, since Divine Canned Knowledge has been in circulation for a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yet, they fled once we were headed to the village, almost as if they knew we were on their trail. Why is that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, yeah, why is that...?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: We may have a mole in our midst.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: One of us could be secretly revealing our whereabouts to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are our friendships that shallow?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like none of you have realized wherein lies the issue.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Care to share your thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Cyno, you're the reason why they can predict our movements.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what's that supposed to mean!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Choose your next words very carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It is simply a logical inference. I have my reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is... Cyno's the mole?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Interesting. And here I thought you were the most suspicious one, Alhaitham, since you were always acting alone.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I know. You have a point, but I realized something as we were returning from the hospital — Cyno isn't like any of us.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you still remember who you are, General Mahamatra?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As a matra, you are no doubt privy to certain kinds of information. Before you can take action against someone, you are required to have all the facts available, including the less-than-savory details.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Simply put, the Akademiya has traditionally allowed you access to a wealth of sensitive information. Knowing their modus operandi, wouldn't you expect them to take precautions against you?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If you want to raise a vicious wolf, you need to make sure that you can avoid its bite.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akademiya is monitoring me?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's not that simple. The Akademiya has eyes all over Sumeru, but they have a special protocol for dealing with you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Every so often comes a Jnagarbha Day. On this day, the Akademiya enters new information into the Akasha through Knowledge Capsules.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I remember seeing the thick notebook next to the control panel once. Its contents were all about the General Mahamatra — his activities throughout the day, preferred methods of enacting judgment... everything.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're saying that the Akademiya entered my information into the Akasha, too?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...But what's the point in doing that? My actions aren't important enough to be added into the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akasha is capable of computation.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akasha's algorithms are entirely capable of predicting your movements using the data entered. When you would depart, the route you would follow, your destination... it knew all of this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It predicted my every move...!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The Akademiya has been watching you longer than you think. However, the fact that you resigned is proof that their suspicions were well-founded.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: So that's how it is... Cyno adheres to his principles so strongly that he's actually a thorn in their side.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Tenacity of will and steadfast faith are worthless to the Akademiya. They need scholars who are easily pliable and mindlessly go after anything they can profit from.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Cyno, don't take it to heart. This just proves how much of a trustworthy ally you are.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They escaped because of me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't blame yourself! It's not like any of us would've known!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...I have an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If they've predicted my movements... then I might be able to guess where they went.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Whoa, you bounced back fast!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There is always an opportunity for safety after danger passes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, so that's how it is! Paimon gets it now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If the Akademiya is trying to avoid Cyno, then the safest place would be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One step behind him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that's right!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They'll want to proceed in the direction opposite of where I'm going.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're getting smarter, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I must go.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: There's also something I want to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go, guys! After 'em!

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Please, wait! I wanna go, too!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Hmm, you want to go, too? If so... you have to promise you'll stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: I wanna find Grandpa! I promise I'll be careful and not cause any trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Everyone, I leave him in your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, let's go! Remember to pack some food with you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like we're missing someone though... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, where do we go from here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cyno, do you remember the route you took?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Yes. After leaving the village, we should head straight toward the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's something here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's this...?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's buried in the sand... Looks like we'll need to roll up our sleeves and do some work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And Paimon thought running around everywhere was already enough work!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now isn't the time for complaining, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay... So we have to dig it out? Whatever's down there looks like it's buried really deep.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With some effort, you manage to retrieve the buried objects.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: These are likely fragments of an Akademiya-developed device, something akin to a headset.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Looks like there were more than one Village Keeper. They must have been escorted this way, because there are device fragments scattered around here...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's split up and search the area. Chances are that we'll find other things nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone goes in different directions and starts digging in the sand.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a short while, you dig up another device nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this what we're searching for? It looks kinda scary...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This is definitely a device used to extract divine knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How did it end up buried in the sand? That can't have been part of the plan.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They must've been attacked along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what!?

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Grandpa... I hope you're okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, your grandpa's gonna be fine!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Razak didn't display any signs of starvation or dehydration, which means that they left fairly recently.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We should be able to catch up.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: One more thing: Given that the device had been entirely covered by sand...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I believe the attack must have happened prior to the sandstorm.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's keep going. They can't have gone far.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't get any closer. They'll notice us.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Dehya's talking with the Eremites? Heh, very interesting... Let's listen in.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...If you had informed me sooner, there'd be plenty of room for us to...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: ...You're one of us... We would never lie...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Scholars... You don't know as much as I do... Need me to...

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Haha, I knew it... That's our Dehya...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Dehya... Why would you...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Dehya!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Didn't you say you'd help me find Grandpa!? Wh—Why are you on their side?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Haha, well, look who's here. Ain't that something.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Ugh, this complicates things.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...You've betrayed Aaru Village?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: So, this is the great General Mahamatra. Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Dehya, you'd be better off as my assistant than hanging around with this motley crew. You've seen for yourself — I have the means and methods, and my ideals are far more admirable than theirs.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I'm not the type that's easily swayed, Rahman. You of all people should know that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what's going on, Dehya? Whose side are you on here?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Shut it, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter. Whichever side you pick, nothing can deter us from the grand mission of resurrecting King Deshret. Once our lord of old returns to this land, we will have a new beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Face the facts, Rahman — it's not gonna happen. You should understand that more than anyone. Have all your years as a merc taught you nothing about placing hopes in a ruler?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: I'm a desert-dweller, and a proud follower of King Deshret. Whether I live by the edge of the sword or in peaceful comfort, my soul will always carry this conviction.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: It's not too late yet. The Village Kee— ...mad scholars aren't gonna bring King Deshret back to life.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You don't understand, my dear lady. Pursuing our faith is our purpose in life. Even if the chance of success is one in a million, we must be willing to give everything we have.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Even if it'll expose you to the Akademiya? Even if they end up disbanding the Eremites? YOUR Eremites, which you've worked so hard for all these years?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: We've waited a long time for this day to come... The sun and the moon no longer shine here. All you see now is cracks in this desiccated land. But, fate has finally dealt me a hand to play against the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: With these scholars in our custody, we'll stomp the Akademiya's forces and fight our way beyond the Wall of Samiel.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Ridiculous. Think about it, the Akademiya controls the entirety of Sumeru. Your powers are negligible in comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: If you still don't believe me, then try asking these two men. They're also against the Akademiya, but neither of them are as arrogant as you are.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Hah, they look more like pawns of the Akademiya to me. Why would I listen to anything the people of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata have to say?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Filthy traitors... Your god abandoned all honor and betrayed King Deshret. We desert-dwellers will never trust the likes of you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's impossible to communicate with someone so hostile.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Perhaps we should...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Do you really believe that by kidnapping the scholars, you'll be able to negotiate with the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: These people have no value as bargaining chips, but I could be persuaded to take their place as your next hostage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: These scholars were exiled from the Akademiya. I, on the other hand, am their current scribe and will be a much greater asset to you.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Wait, you can't be serious.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: So, you wanna trade places with the hostages, do ya?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Precisely. Any wise person would gladly accept my offer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What're you thinking!? What if they decide to kill you instead?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, that would be bad luck for me.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: However, I'd get the chance to observe the scholars — perhaps even find out the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Think you can talk me over with that confident look of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm not trying to persuade you. I'm using this as a means of joining forces against the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You are their scribe. What do you have against the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not all desert-dwellers believe in King Deshret, and the same applies to the Akademiya. Why must all knowledge-seekers approve of the Akademiya's way of doing things?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Hah... hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You Akademiya scum! Every last one of you is nothing but a hypocrite, just like everyone else on the other side of that wall! I've made myself clear enough... I won't listen to another word from the Dendro Archon's people.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Not so fast.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Alhaitham, do you stand by everything you just said?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I never make empty promises.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You know you're making a dangerous decision, right?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Good! Rahman, hear me out. These people are my friends. Maybe you can't take the followers of the Dendro Archon at their word, but what about me? Do you trust me?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: We've known each other for years. Of course I do.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: In that case, I'm willing to vouch for their honesty with my right arm.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Come on, Rahman, don't be a coward. If you're serious about taking on the Akademiya, you need to steel yourself. You can't be afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Ha! An arm from the Flame-Mane? You've piqued my interest.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: But what if you refuse to oblige? What should I do then? No one's a fool here, Dehya. We're mercs. And mercs don't tend to live long unless they have their wits about them.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You're not wrong, but this is different. I promised my friends that we'd bring back the Village Keepers together.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Hah! Let's do it right here then. Give me your right arm as proof of your resolve.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't listen to him! He's not even trying to negotiate, he just wants to make things more difficult!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...That's fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you crazy!?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: We came here to save lives. One arm for that many people is still a pretty good deal if you ask me. Rahman, I'm holding up my end of the deal here. You'd better not let me down.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Sure. Go ahead and cut off her right arm.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: No!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya! What are you gonna do? Think of something!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...You don't have to go this far.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: That's not for you to decide.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Do it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dehya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dehya, run!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Huh!

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Stop!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...What's wrong? Can't do it?

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: Flame-Mane, you and I are both desert folk. Cutting off your arm is no different than cutting off my own fingers. Where's the sense in cutting my own kin to pieces?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tch.

dialogues.speaker: Rahman
dialogues.text: You've shown me that you're serious. Go on now, take your friends and leave. Meet me in the desert at noon tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Phew!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I was really counting on him not going through with it.

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: Dehya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was crazy! Have you all lost your minds!? What if he'd actually cut your arm off!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hmm, then I'd just have to hold my claymore with my left arm.

choices.text: Please don't do that ever again!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Okay, I'm sorry... But sometimes when you're out on a limb, you gotta double down to seal the deal, you know?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Don't ever make a promise like that again. I can deal with the likes of them.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: If it came down to it, you would not lose to them either.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: I don't doubt it, Cyno, but this is about more than me and them... There's a lot more where they came from.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Even if we got rid of one bunch of radicals, there are others out there. Wiping them out would do more harm than good.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ah... As you wish.

response.speaker: Isak
response.text: I'm sorry, Dehya! I should've stayed put and listened... I should've trusted you...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: It's okay. I promised you I'd help find your grandpa, so I'll do whatever it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You look worried. Thinking about the Village Keepers?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes... I'd look for them myself if I could... As members of our village, each one of them is very important to me.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You have a strong sense of belonging here... I guess I'm the opposite. Mercs are stray dogs wherever they go.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Dehya, don't say that. You can be a part of this community, too.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Haha, thanks. I'll let you know when I feel like joining.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Anpu
dialogues.text: *sigh* I just hope everyone's alright.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What scheme is the Akademiya brewing now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this the place? It's in terrible shape... and there's sand everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Empty and forgotten. An ideal place to hide people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaah, monsters! Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, but running on sand is sooo tiring...

dialogues.speaker: Isak
dialogues.text: But... you're flying, aren't you, Paimon? Is flying over sand tiring too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaagh, of course it is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, that looks like Dehya! What's she doing here!?
